# Test for qmpEventHandler fix - verifies no log flooding on VM stop/start cycles
#
# This test validates the fix for the QMP event handler race condition that caused
# log flooding (~10,000 messages/sec) when a VM was stopped and restarted.
#
# The bug occurred because:
# 1. Old QMP handler's event channel gets closed when VM stops
# 2. VM restarts with same domain name (UUID.Version.AppNum unchanged)
# 3. New VM creates QMP socket at same path
# 4. Old handler's os.Stat() passes (new file exists)
# 5. Old handler's closed channel returns zero values in tight loop
#
# The fix uses 'for range eventChan' which exits cleanly when channel closes.
# Success indicator: log message "Event channel closed for socket"
# Failure indicator: flood of "Unhandled event:" with empty event name
#
# NO SPECIAL PREREQUISITES - just needs Eden with EVE running.

{{$network_name := "n1"}}
{{$app_name := "qmp-test-vm"}}
{{$cycles := "5"}}
{{define "image"}}https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img{{end}}

[!exec:bash] stop
[!exec:sleep] stop

# Cleanup from any previous interrupted test run
message 'Cleaning up any leftover resources from previous runs'
exec -t 2m bash cleanup-previous.sh {{$app_name}} {{$network_name}}

# Create network
eden -t 1m network create 10.11.12.0/24 -n {{$network_name}}
test eden.network.test -test.v -timewait 2m ACTIVATED {{$network_name}}

# Deploy a simple VM (FML mode for OVMF/UEFI boot)
message 'Deploying test VM'
exec -t 5m bash deploy-test-vm.sh {{$app_name}} {{$network_name}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 20m RUNNING {{$app_name}}

# Run multiple stop/start cycles to trigger the race condition
message 'Running {{$cycles}} stop/start cycles to trigger QMP handler race condition'
exec -t 60m bash run-stop-start-cycles.sh {{$app_name}} {{$cycles}}
stdout 'All cycles completed successfully'

# Check logs for success or failure indicators
message 'Checking EVE logs for fix verification'
exec -t 2m bash check-qmp-fix.sh

# Cleanup
eden pod delete {{$app_name}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 10m - {{$app_name}}

eden network delete {{$network_name}}
test eden.network.test -test.v -timewait 10m - {{$network_name}}

-- eden-config.yml --
{{/* Test's config file */}}
test:
    controller: adam://{{EdenConfig "adam.ip"}}:{{EdenConfig "adam.port"}}
    eve:
      {{EdenConfig "eve.name"}}:
        onboard-cert: {{EdenConfigPath "eve.cert"}}
        serial: "{{EdenConfig "eve.serial"}}"
        model: {{EdenConfig "eve.devmodel"}}

-- cleanup-previous.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Clean up resources from previous interrupted test runs
# Usage: cleanup-previous.sh <app_name> <network_name>
# This script is idempotent - safe to run even if resources don't exist

APP_NAME=$1
NETWORK_NAME=$2
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}

echo "=== Cleaning up previous test resources ==="

# Check if pod exists and delete it
if $EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${APP_NAME}[[:space:]]"; then
    echo "Found existing pod '$APP_NAME', deleting..."
    $EDEN pod delete "$APP_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true

    # Wait for pod to be fully deleted (up to 2 minutes)
    echo "Waiting for pod deletion..."
    for i in $(seq 1 120); do
        if ! $EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${APP_NAME}[[:space:]]"; then
            echo "  Pod deleted after ${i}s"
            break
        fi
        sleep 1
    done
else
    echo "No existing pod '$APP_NAME' found"
fi

# Check if network exists and delete it
if $EDEN network ls 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${NETWORK_NAME}[[:space:]]"; then
    echo "Found existing network '$NETWORK_NAME', deleting..."
    $EDEN network delete "$NETWORK_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true

    # Wait for network to be fully deleted (up to 1 minute)
    echo "Waiting for network deletion..."
    for i in $(seq 1 60); do
        if ! $EDEN network ls 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${NETWORK_NAME}[[:space:]]"; then
            echo "  Network deleted after ${i}s"
            break
        fi
        sleep 1
    done
else
    echo "No existing network '$NETWORK_NAME' found"
fi

echo "Cleanup complete"

-- deploy-test-vm.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Deploy test VM for QMP handler testing
# Usage: deploy-test-vm.sh <app_name> <network_name>

set -e

APP_NAME=$1
NETWORK_NAME=$2
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
IMAGE="https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img"

echo "=== Deploying test VM: $APP_NAME ==="
echo "Network: $NETWORK_NAME"
echo "Image: $IMAGE"

# Deploy VM in FML mode (uses OVMF/UEFI firmware)
$EDEN pod deploy -n "$APP_NAME" --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 -p 8028:22 "$IMAGE" --networks="$NETWORK_NAME"

echo "VM deployment initiated"

-- run-stop-start-cycles.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Run multiple stop/start cycles on a VM to trigger QMP handler race condition
#
# Usage: run-stop-start-cycles.sh <app_name> <num_cycles>

set -e

APP_NAME=$1
NUM_CYCLES=${2:-20}
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}

# Function to get pod state - extracts LAST_STATE(EVE) which is what EVE actually reports
get_pod_state() {
    local name=$1
    # eden pod ps output is tab-separated:
    # NAME\tIMAGE\tUUID\tINTERNAL\tEXTERNAL\tMEMORY\tSTATE(ADAM)\tLAST_STATE(EVE)
    # Use rev|cut|rev to reliably get the last tab-separated field
    $EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | grep "^${name}[[:space:]]" | head -1 | rev | cut -f1 | rev
}

echo "=== Running $NUM_CYCLES stop/start cycles on $APP_NAME ==="

for i in $(seq 1 $NUM_CYCLES); do
    echo ""
    echo "=== Cycle $i/$NUM_CYCLES ==="

    # Stop the VM
    echo "Stopping $APP_NAME..."
    $EDEN pod stop "$APP_NAME"

    # Wait for HALTED state (Ubuntu VM typically halts within 60-120 seconds)
    echo "Waiting for HALTED state..."
    STATE=""
    for j in $(seq 1 300); do
        STATE=$(get_pod_state "$APP_NAME")
        if [ "$STATE" = "HALTED" ]; then
            echo "  State: HALTED (after ${j}s)"
            break
        fi
        if [ $j -eq 1 ] || [ $((j % 30)) -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "  Attempt $j: state='$STATE'"
        fi
        sleep 1
    done

    if [ "$STATE" != "HALTED" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: VM did not reach HALTED state (current: $STATE)"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Start the VM
    echo "Starting $APP_NAME..."
    $EDEN pod start "$APP_NAME"

    # Wait for RUNNING state
    echo "Waiting for RUNNING state..."
    STATE=""
    for j in $(seq 1 120); do
        STATE=$(get_pod_state "$APP_NAME")
        if [ "$STATE" = "RUNNING" ]; then
            echo "  State: RUNNING (after ${j}s)"
            break
        fi
        if [ $j -eq 1 ] || [ $((j % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "  Attempt $j: state='$STATE'"
        fi
        sleep 1
    done

    if [ "$STATE" != "RUNNING" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: VM did not reach RUNNING state (current: $STATE)"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Check for log flooding after each cycle (check EVE logs directly)
    # Logs are in /persist/newlog/collect/dev.log.* files
    EMPTY_EVENTS=$($EDEN eve ssh "cat /persist/newlog/collect/dev.log.* 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null | grep -c "Unhandled event:  from QMP socket" || true)
    if [ "$EMPTY_EVENTS" -gt 100 ]; then
        echo ""
        echo "EARLY FAILURE: Detected $EMPTY_EVENTS empty event messages after cycle $i"
        echo "QMP handler bug is present!"
        exit 1
    fi

    echo "Cycle $i complete. Empty events so far: $EMPTY_EVENTS"
done

echo ""
echo "All cycles completed successfully"
echo "No log flooding detected during $NUM_CYCLES stop/start cycles"

-- check-qmp-fix.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Check EVE logs to verify the QMP handler fix is working
#
# Success: "Event channel closed for socket" messages (fix working)
# Failure: Many "Unhandled event:" with empty event name (bug present)
#
# We check logs directly on EVE (/persist/newlog) because:
# - The success message uses logrus.Infof (info level)
# - Remote log level to Adam may filter out info messages
# - Local EVE logs contain all levels

set -e

EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
THRESHOLD=100  # More than this many empty events = failure

echo "=== Checking QMP handler fix ==="

# Get logs directly from EVE's /persist/newlog/collect
# This contains all log levels, not filtered by remote log level
echo "Fetching logs directly from EVE..."
LOGS=$($EDEN eve ssh "cat /persist/newlog/collect/dev.log.* 2>/dev/null; zcat /persist/newlog/keepSentQueue/*.gz 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null | grep -i qmpEventHandler || true)

if [ -z "$LOGS" ]; then
    echo "Warning: No qmpEventHandler logs found in EVE local logs"
    echo "Trying Adam logs as fallback..."
    LOGS=$($EDEN log --format=json 'content:qmpEventHandler' 2>/dev/null || true)
fi

# Count success indicators (fix working correctly)
# The fix logs: "Event channel closed for socket: ... (QMP connection lost)"
SUCCESS_COUNT=$(echo "$LOGS" | grep -c "Event channel closed for socket" || true)

# Count failure indicators (empty "Unhandled event:" messages)
# The bug produces: "qmpEventHandler: Unhandled event:  from QMP socket"
# Note the double space after "event:" - that's the empty event name
EMPTY_EVENT_COUNT=$(echo "$LOGS" | grep -c "Unhandled event:  from QMP socket" || true)

echo "Success indicators (channel closed messages): $SUCCESS_COUNT"
echo "Failure indicators (empty event messages): $EMPTY_EVENT_COUNT"

if [ "$EMPTY_EVENT_COUNT" -gt "$THRESHOLD" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "FAIL: Detected $EMPTY_EVENT_COUNT empty event messages (threshold: $THRESHOLD)"
    echo "The QMP handler bug is present - log flooding occurred!"
    echo ""
    echo "Sample of empty event messages:"
    echo "$LOGS" | grep "Unhandled event:  from" | head -5
    exit 1
fi

if [ "$SUCCESS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "PASS: Found $SUCCESS_COUNT 'Event channel closed' messages"
    echo "The QMP handler fix is working correctly!"
    echo ""
    echo "Sample success messages:"
    echo "$LOGS" | grep "Event channel closed" | head -3
    exit 0
fi

# If we got here with few/no empty events and no success messages,
# it's still a pass - the important thing is no flooding
if [ "$EMPTY_EVENT_COUNT" -le "$THRESHOLD" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "PASS: No log flooding detected ($EMPTY_EVENT_COUNT empty events, threshold: $THRESHOLD)"
    echo "Note: 'Event channel closed' message may not appear if race condition wasn't triggered"
    exit 0
fi

echo ""
echo "INCONCLUSIVE: Unable to determine test result"
exit 1
